content.comment_body: Does [company_name] have a 'Wish List' for features or functions that end users want in upcoming products? I would really appreciate a way to reference a start value in an up/down counter. I can reference the other two parameters but, oddly, not the one I need.

Hello [user_name], Are you referring to the [product_name]? Currently, I don't think there's a public list like this on our technical forum. However, I've shared your thread with someone responsible for this [product_name]. If the feature doesn't exist yet (I couldn't verify), maybe this could be considered for the future. Best regards CS Moderator
Thank you for your response. As an end user trying to persuade my employer to adopt the [product_name]/PLC approach, it is frustrating when intuitive features are missing. But I remain hopeful.
[url] It's an old post! But you can start a new one. We began discussing this before the [version_no] series launched and saw some wishes come true. Best regards
I agree! This is a good suggestion, [company_name] should consider implementing it.

Dear Users, Every product manager likely maintains a list of possible new functions, but these lists are not made public. Deciding which function to implement first is up to them. Feel free to share your ideas here. We will do our best to forward them to the appropriate person so that nothing is overlooked. Best regards CS Moderator

I suggest we add our feature requests for [product_name] [article_no] to the spreadsheet at the end of the [article_no] wishlist thread. It would be fantastic to see the evolution of [product_name] in this manner. [article_no] still feels fresh, and it's valuable to compare its capabilities with user wishes.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users want clearer ways to make and track requests for new functions in [product_name], noting that current communication leaves uncertainty about feature consideration. A specific missing feature—referencing a start value in up/down counters—is cited as particularly frustrating. Feedback highlights the desire for more transparency and features that closely meet end user requirements.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the product to allow referencing all counter parameters, especially the start value, and wish for a transparent, official channel to submit and follow requests for new features.
